issue.title: A counsel status question can poison an active build with a foreign commit
issue.body:
Severity: high / Provenance: product

## Problem

Item 229’s executor committed the requested implementation at `15a774515f5a`. While build-01 was still active, `counsel --ask "how is it going so far?"` wrote counsel-01 and the driver committed it at `24aed171c5ec`. On the executor’s next return, `cmd_build` correctly found that driver-authored commit between `start_sha` and HEAD and refused the build as `no-cause`.

The operator’s read-only status question therefore changed the active build’s HEAD and invalidated an otherwise executor-authored build. The green forge checks do not cure this race, and the selected-test failure does not explain the recorded refusal.

## Retires

A read-only counsel/status inquiry, or transport of its record, being able to introduce a foreign commit into an active build’s commit range.

## Change

Make counsel/status recording and transport unable to mutate the checkout observed by an active build. Use an isolated transport worktree or defer the counsel-record commit until the active stage has produced its record. Preserve the build’s foreign-author guard; driver commits must not be silently exempted from it.

## Acceptance

- Start a two-iteration build whose first iteration creates an executor-authored commit and whose second iteration is still running.
- Run `attavo counsel N --ask "how is it going so far?"` and transport its record during that interval.
- The active build’s HEAD and executor commit range remain unchanged by the counsel operation.
- The build is not refused for the counsel record and can pass after its gates pass.
- The counsel record is eventually committed by the driver without being lost.
- An actual non-executor commit introduced into the build’s range remains refused by the existing authorship guard.
